Togo's Faure Gnassingbé Celebrates the "Correct the Map" Resolution Amid Domestic Criticism

2026-09-13 Togo Actualité Togo, Faure Gnassingbé, Correct the Map, UN resolution, Equal Earth, Africa, cartography, world map, cognitive justice
Read the source article

Quick summary

Togolese President Faure Gnassingbé has championed the UN's "Correct the Map" resolution as a triumph for Africa, but critics at home dismiss the celebration as a distraction from two decades of domestic infrastructure failure and political stagnation.

Key takeaways

  • Togo's President Faure Gnassingbé and Foreign Minister Robert Dussey have positioned themselves as champions of the UN "Correct the Map" resolution
  • Critics argue the regime is using the cartographic victory to distract from 20 years of domestic stagnation in infrastructure, healthcare, and development
  • The article contrasts Togo's lack of modernization with progress in neighboring West African countries like Benin, Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, and Ghana
  • Togo's railway network remains the colonial-era infrastructure, and the promised highway was never built
  • The piece highlights the irony of celebrating global cartographic correction while the country's own social and physical landscape remains frozen in the 1960s
  • The "Correct the Map" movement is framed as a demagogic project by leaders unable to solve concrete citizen problems
